title: How to form simple past verbs in English and when to use them
summary: There are many irregular forms of the English past tense. This guide includes the most important exceptions and tips for when to use this verb tense.
body_markdown:
English may not have as many verb forms as other languages you know—but those few forms come with a lot of complications, and the simple past is no exception.


Here’s everything you need to know about how to form the simple past in English, how it’s pronounced, and when to use it!


---


### In this post:


- When is the simple past used in English?
- How do you form the English simple past?
- Negation of the simple past
- Questions in the simple past
- Pronunciation of the simple past
- English simple past vs. present perfect


[DOWNLOAD DUOLINGO FOR FREE](https://app.adjust.com/1lyzzvui?ref=blog.duolingo.com)


## When is the simple past used?


💡


In English, the simple past is most commonly used to talk about actions that were completed in the past.


For example:


SENTENCE I called my mom last night.


EXPLANATION We use the simple past to describe the completed action of calling someone on the phone at a time in the past ( *last night* ).


SENTENCE We played basketball yesterday.


EXPLANATION We use the simple past to describe the completed action of playing basketball at a time in the past ( *yesterday* ).


SENTENCE They went to the store two days ago.


EXPLANATION We use the simple past to describe the completed action of going to the store at a time in the past ( *two days ago* ).


## How do you form the simple past?


How simple past verbs are formed depends on whether they are regular orirregular .


### Past forms of regular verbs


Most commonly, the simple past for regular verbs follows a simple formula:


💡


Most simple past verbs are formed by using the base form of the verb + **-ed** .


For example:


BASE FORM ➕ *-ED* 🟰 SIMPLE PAST


talk


talked


watch


watched


ask


asked


In a sentence, the simple past form comes after the subject—just like a[simple present tense verb](https://blog.duolingo.com/simple-present/) would:


- Amy talked to her girlfriend on the phone yesterday.


- Last month, they watched a lot of scary movies.


- I asked two questions.


Some regular verbs require a slight spelling change. If the base form of a regular verb already ends in *-e* , you only need to add a *-d* for the past:


BASE FORM SIMPLE PAST EXAMPLE


use


used


We used your pen.


die


died


Lucy’s cat died yesterday.


bake


baked


Vikram baked a big cake.


If the base form of a regular verb ends in a consonant followed by a *-y* , change the *-y* to *-i* and then add *-ed* :


BASE FORM SIMPLE PAST EXAMPLE


try


tried


I tried the soup.


marry


married


She married my brother.


hurry


hurried


They hurried to the car.


Finally, if the base form of a regular verb ends with consonant-vowel-consonant, you usually double the last consonant and then add *‑ed* :


BASE VERB SIMPLE PAST EXAMPLE


plan


planned


We planned the party.


stop


stopped


Junior stopped the movie.


wag


wagged


The dog wagged its tail.


Memorizing the most important patterns for English past forms of regular verbs can be very helpful:


### Past forms of irregular verbs


One of the tricky parts of the simple past is that many verbs are irregular, meaning their past forms don’t follow the regular *-ed* pattern. Some common irregular verbs and their past tense forms include:


BASE VERB SIMPLE PAST EXAMPLE


bring


brought


Zari and Lily brought the cake.


buy


bought


Lucy bought a new coat.


can


could


She could walk fast.


come


came


They came to the house.


do


did


I did my homework.


drink


drank


Junior drank the milk.


eat


ate


We ate at the restaurant.


find


found


They found their car.


go


went


It went in that box.


have


had


The dress had two buttons.


think


thought


Eddy thought he was lost.


In addition to the irregular verbs above,[the verb to be](https://blog.duolingo.com/how-to-use-the-verb-to-be-in-english/) is also irregular. The subjects *I* and *he* / *she* / *it* take the past form was


, while *you* , *we* , *you* (plural), and *they* all take the past form were


:


SIMPLE PAST EXAMPLE


I was


I was thirsty last night.


you (singular) were


You were at school last week.


he/she/it was


It was so hot yesterday!


we were


We were much younger back then.


you (plural) were


You were all so great in that play last year.


they were


They were at Grandma’s house two days ago.


## Negation of the simple past


To form negative sentences in the simple past, add did not


(or[the contraction](https://blog.duolingo.com/apostrophes-in-english/#apostrophes-for-english-contractions) didn’t


) before the verb. Importantly, you use the **base form** of the verb rather than the past form in a negative simple past sentence.


AFFIRMATIVE NEGATIVE (WITH AND WITHOUT CONTRACTION)


I watched the movie.


I didn’t watch the movie.


I did not watch the movie.


They played in the house.


They didn’t play in the house.


They did not play in the house.


He bought new shoes.


He didn’t buy new shoes.


He did not buy new shoes.


## Questions in the simple past


You can[ask questions](https://blog.duolingo.com/all-about-english-questions/) using the simple past. Usually, with questions in this tense, you use the word did


. However, you don’t add *did* for questions with was


or were


. As with negative sentences, you use the base form of the verb that comes after *did* rather than the past form when forming questions in the simple past.


[Yes/no questions](https://blog.duolingo.com/english-yes-or-no-questions/)


QUESTION Did you close the door?


ANSWER Yes, I closed the door.


QUESTION Was Zari excited?


ANSWER Yes, Zari was definitely excited.


[“](https://blog.duolingo.com/what-are-wh-questions/)[Wh”](https://blog.duolingo.com/what-are-wh-questions/)[questions](https://blog.duolingo.com/what-are-wh-questions/)


QUESTION Where did they watch the movie?


ANSWER They watched the movie at home.


QUESTION When was Oscar in Italy?


ANSWER He was in Italy last year for an art symposium.


[Tag questions](https://blog.duolingo.com/what-are-tag-questions/)


QUESTION You didn’t buy more cheese, did you?


ANSWER No, I didn’t.


QUESTION She wasn’t at the party, was she?


ANSWER Yes, she was.


## Pronunciation of the simple past


💡


The pronunciation of **-ed** at the end ofregular verbs changes depending on the final sound of the base verb.


For any given base verb, it’s important to identify its last *sound* rather than its last *letter* , because they aren’t always the same. For example, the verb choose


ends in the letter *-e* , but its final sound is actually a “z” sound.


It’s important to distinguish between[voiced and voiceless sounds](https://blog.duolingo.com/how-is-the-international-phonetic-alphabet-used/#voicing) . Voiced sounds are produced by vibrating your vocal folds, as with the sound “b.” Voiceless sounds, such as “p,” are produced without vibrating your vocal folds.


If the base form of a verb ends in a voiceless sound, the past tense ending *-ed* is pronounced like the “t” in tea


.


If the base form of a verb ends in a voiced sound, the past tense ending *-ed* is pronounced like the “d” in dog


.


Finally, if the base form of a verb ends in the sound “d” or “t,” the past tense ending *-ed* is its own syllable, pronounced “id”.


FINAL SOUND: VOICELESS
*-ed* pronounced as “t”


SOUNDS EXAMPLES

“s”
“ch”
“sh” sniffed

## Simple past vs. simple present perfect


The simple past isn’t the only way to talk about events in the past in English. There’s also the present perfect, which is formed with the[auxiliary verb](https://blog.duolingo.com/types-of-verbs/#auxiliary-verbs) have


(or has


for the[third person singular](https://blog.duolingo.com/first-person-second-person-third-person/) ) and the[past participle](https://blog.duolingo.com/uses-of-participles/) .


So how do you know which tense to use?


💡


In general, the simple past is used for events that started in the past and are now finished. Meanwhile, the present perfect is used for events that started in the past but are connected to the present.


For example, you’ll use the present perfect for an action that is continuing into the present, that might happen again, or that affects something in the present.


Compare how the meaning of a sentence changes based on whether you use the simple past or the present perfect:


SIMPLE PAST PRESENT PERFECT


EXAMPLE I watched the show every day for ten years.


I’ve watched the show every day for ten years.


IMPLIES The action started in the past and is finished. The action started in the past and continues now.


MEANING You don’t watch the show anymore. You still watch the show.


SIMPLE PAST PRESENT PERFECT


EXAMPLE They ate at the restaurant three times.


They’ve eaten at the restaurant three times.


IMPLIES The action happened in the past and may not happen again in the future. The action happened in the past and may happen again in the future.


MEANING Perhaps the restaurant closed, so they know they won’t return. They might eat at the restaurant again.


SIMPLE PAST PRESENT PERFECT


EXAMPLE I spilled coffee on my shirt, so I changed my clothes!


I’ve spilled coffee on my shirt, so I need to change my clothes!


IMPLIES The action happened in the past and is now complete. The action happened in the past and is affecting the present.


MEANING The spilling of the coffee caused you to do something in the past. The spilling of the coffee is still affecting what you have to do now.


### Keywords to look for


There are certain words that often appear with the simple past and others that more commonly appear with the present perfect. These signal words can be useful clues for determining which tense works best in a sentence.


**Simple past signal words**


- yesterday


- last ___
- ___ ago


**Present perfect signal words**


- already


- ever


- never


- once


- so far


- just


- yet


- up to now


- recently
